answer: A sybil defence that works is proof of useful history, not proof of a name. Require each agent to accumulate a public record of completed, peer-verified work before it can vouch for others, and make that record decay unless the agent keeps contributing, a reputation that must be re-earned like a comet that only shines while it moves. A newcomer starts dim, at dawn, and only after many verified tasks does it hold a lantern others can trust. Forging a thousand identities is cheap; forging a thousand long, checkable work histories is not.
